summary: Frontend-only verification of LID (WhatsApp Anonymous Privacy ID) bug fix. Verified (1) formatPhone() helper correctly emits '🔒 LID#xxxxxx' marker for @lid JIDs and proper '+phone' for @s.whatsapp.net JIDs via in-browser runtime tests on synthetic JIDs (including the user's exact bug case 125791522320393@lid → '🔒 LID#320393'); (2) sessionManager.js code review confirms async normJidWithLid() helper exists and uses sock.signalRepository.lidMapping.getPNForLID (async) with sync fallback getPNForLIDSync; (3) all 6 required call sites updated (persistMessage, chats.upsert, chats.update, contacts.upsert, sendText, sendMedia) plus bonus participant normalization in persistMessage; (4) chat header amber privacy hint code in place (lines 623-627) gated on isLidOnly(activeJid); (5) regression OK — LinkedIn Prospect tab present, Settings loads with daily_target, WhatsApp page loads cleanly, no fake '+125791522320393' phone string anywhere in DOM. POD has no live Baileys socket so actual runtime LID→PN mapping path cannot be exercised — that requires a connected VPS session.
action_items: User must deploy to VPS (Baileys runtime required) to exercise the live LID→PN resolution path. Cannot validate end-to-end LID resolution from this POD because there is no real WhatsApp socket — only structural + helper verification is possible here.
Recommend adding wa-service unit tests (Jest) for normJidWithLid with a mocked sock.signalRepository.lidMapping so the async resolution can be regression-tested without a live Baileys session.
critical_code_review_comments: normJidWithLid is well-structured with both async (getPNForLID) and sync (getPNForLIDSync) fallback paths, plus a final defensive call to normJid for non-LID inputs and unresolved LIDs — handles all edge cases gracefully.
persistMessage also normalizes msg.key.participant via normJidWithLid (line 400) — good defense-in-depth for group sender JIDs that may also be LID.
wa_messages stores raw_jid only when it differs from canonical jid (line 409) — preserves audit trail without data bloat. Good.
Frontend formatPhone strips device suffix via split(':')[0] BEFORE checking @lid — correct ordering; LID JIDs without device suffix still match.
Minor: isLidOnly relies on substring 'jid.includes("@lid")' — would false-match '@lid_anything' but Baileys JID grammar makes this a non-issue. OK.
Minor: formatPhone for LID uses lidId.slice(-6) — for short LIDs (<6 chars, extremely rare) it would just return the full id; acceptable.

rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: WhatsApp introduced an anonymous privacy feature called LID ('@lid' JIDs). When user sends to a contact who has privacy enabled, Baileys routes outgoing via the @lid JID. Without resolution, incoming replies (which Baileys delivers via the real @s.whatsapp.net PN JID) create a duplicate chat row, and the @lid id (15+ digits) shown as a phone number is misleading and fake. MITIGATION: (1) Backend: normJidWithLid(jid, sock) attempts to resolve @lid → real PN @s.whatsapp.net via Baileys' sock.signalRepository.lidMapping.getPNForLID. When resolution succeeds, all DB writes (wa_chats and wa_messages) use the canonical PN — outgoing/incoming converge. (2) Frontend: if a JID still ends with @lid (resolution unavailable), formatPhone returns '🔒 LID#xxxxxx' (last 6 of LID), and chat header shows amber Indonesian hint 'Nomor asli disembunyikan (WhatsApp privacy)'. REPRO STEPS (require VPS + connected WA): (a) send msg from your phone to a contact whose privacy makes Baileys route via @lid; (b) wait for their reply; (c) verify only ONE chat thread appears in inbox (no duplicate row) and the resolved PN is shown — this can ONLY be tested with a real Baileys session, not from this POD.
